suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The Meet fallback dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar even when destinationCalendar is null or empty. WHY: Bookings selecting Google Meet without a destination calendar now throw instead of falling back to Cal Video, including the null destination produced by handleNewBooking. HOW: Restore the optional access on the integration check.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Office365 event creation always selects the first host's destination calendar, ignoring the credential for the current provider instance. WHY: EventManager now invokes this method for every collective host with the same full destination array, so a secondary Office365 host sends its token with the primary host's calendar ID and fails to create its event. HOW: Accept the credentialId supplied by CalendarManager and select the matching destination.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Reference creation now removes credentialId from every non-calendar result, including dedicated video meetings. WHY: createMeeting returns the video credential ID, and handleCancelBooking only deletes the video meeting when its reference has that ID, so newly booked video meetings remain active after cancellation. HOW: Preserve result.credentialId for video results as well.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The fallback searches destination calendars for an externalId equal to the missing externalCalendarId. WHY: For references without an external calendar ID, update sends an undefined calendarId and deletion falls back to primary instead of the configured non-primary calendar, breaking legacy booking updates and cancellations. HOW: Restore the first destination's externalId as the single-calendar fallback in both updateEvent and deleteEvent.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Collective host destinations are appended with optional chaining to a destination array that can be null. WHY: When the organizer and event type have no destination but another collective host does, that host's configured calendar is silently discarded and EventManager never creates its calendar event. HOW: Initialize an empty array before appending the other hosts' destinations.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Recurring cancellation ignores the credential resolved for the current host reference and again loops only over the organizer's credentials using the first calendar reference. WHY: With the newly supported multiple collective calendar references, cancelling all remaining occurrences repeatedly deletes the organizer's events but leaves secondary hosts' recurring events in their calendars. HOW: Use the resolved calendar for the current reference and select each updated booking's reference by that credentialId instead of taking its first calendar reference.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The first destination belongs to the main organizer, not necessarily to the credential used by this service. createAllCalendarEvents now calls createEvent for every collective host's credential while passing the same destination array. For a second Office365 host, this therefore requests /me/calendars/<organizer-calendar-id>/events using the second host's token, typically failing with a calendar-not-found error instead of creating their event. Select the destination matching the credentialId passed by CalendarManager rather than always taking element zero.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now iterates all collective hosts' destination calendars and calls createEvent with each host's credential; CalendarManager passes that credential ID to the provider while retaining the entire destinationCalendar array. This implementation always takes element zero, so a second Office365 host's token is used against the first host's calendar ID (potentially even a Google calendar ID in a mixed-provider event). Creation fails or targets the wrong calendar, while the saved reference records the second host's intended external ID. Accept the credential ID and select the destination matching it, as the Google implementation now does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When a Google Meet booking has no destination calendar, the destructured first element is undefined (handleNewBooking explicitly constructs a null destination in this case). Accessing its integration throws instead of falling back to Cal Video, aborting booking creation. Preserve the optional access used before the array migration.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: createAllCalendarEvents now calls this method once per destination credential but passes the entire event destination array each time. Selecting element zero means a second Office365 host attempts to create in the organizer's calendar using the second host's token. Normally Graph rejects that calendar ID, leaving the collective host without an event; if accessible, the event is created in the wrong calendar while the reference records the second host's external ID. Select the destination matching the credential passed by CalendarManager rather than always using the first destination.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new array destructuring yields an undefined first element for null or empty destinations, but the fallback now dereferences it without optional chaining. handleNewBooking explicitly produces null when neither event type nor organizer has a destination. With Google Meet selected, this throws instead of preserving the previous fallback to Cal Video.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: EventManager now passes the entire destination array to each host's calendar service, and CalendarManager supplies that host's credential ID. This consumer still takes only the first destination. For a second Office365 host it therefore requests the organizer's calendar ID using the second host's token, typically failing creation or writing to the wrong calendar if shared access exists. Accept the credentialId argument and select its matching destination, as the Google provider does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The reference mapping previously preserved result.credentialId for non-calendar results. Changing the false branch to undefined drops the video/conferencing credential identity, even though moving calendar credential IDs into EventResult does not change the non-calendar contract. Preserve result.credentialId for both kinds so later operations can identify the integration account that created the meeting.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: EventManager now iterates all collective destinations and invokes this service with each destination's credential, but this method always selects destinationCalendar[0]. For a second Office365 host, the request uses that host's token with the organizer's calendar ID, typically failing to create their event (or targeting the wrong calendar). Select the destination matching the credential passed by CalendarManager rather than always taking the first entry.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The fallback executes only when externalCalendarId is falsy, but then searches for a destination whose externalId equals that same falsy value. A normal configured destination cannot match. Updates to legacy references without an external calendar ID therefore lose the previously working destination fallback; the analogous delete fallback now targets primary instead of the configured calendar. Use a usable destination externalId when the reference does not supply one.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This mapping previously retained result.credentialId for non-calendar results; it now explicitly writes undefined for them. Video integration results therefore lose their credential association when converted to booking references, even though the producer supplies it. Preserve result.credentialId for non-calendar results as well as calendar results.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new catch treats PrismaClientKnownRequestError as a client-safe error and copies its raw message into HttpError. Prisma diagnostics can include internal database/query context and offending values, so a failed user lookup can disclose those details through the public booking error response. Preserve explicitly safe HttpError messages, but return a generic message for Prisma failures and keep any necessary diagnostics in appropriately sanitized internal logging.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The admin-or-owner check requires both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner to succeed. WHY: isTeamAdmin accepts ADMIN and OWNER memberships, but isTeamOwner accepts only OWNER, so a team admin who is not the booking organizer or an attendee receives FORBIDDEN. HOW: Use the existing isTeamAdmin result alone, since it already includes owners.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Blacklist enforcement compares the raw guest email against lowercased blacklist entries. WHY: An authorized attendee can add a blocked address using different casing, and the base-email normalization used by handleNewBooking is also bypassed, allowing blocked recipients to receive booking invitations. HOW: Apply the same extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase() normalization used in handleNewBooking before checking the blacklist.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: uniqueGuests only removes existing attendees and does not deduplicate the incoming guests array. WHY: A direct mutation with the same valid address twice passes the server schema and inserts two Attendee rows because that model has no booking/email uniqueness constraint, resulting in duplicate guest entries and notifications despite the dialog's uniqueness validation. HOW: Deduplicate the input before filtering and inserting it, and enforce uniqueness in the server schema rather than relying on the dialog.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Blacklist entries are lowercased, but `guest` retains the casing supplied by the caller: neither the server schema nor the dialog normalizes it. With `blocked@example.com` in BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS, submitting `Blocked@example.com` passes this filter and is persisted and invited. Normalize the candidate before the blacklist comparison so case variations cannot bypass the block.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The filter only checks each guest against the attendees loaded before the request; it does not deduplicate the incoming array. A direct mutation with guests: ["new@example.com", "new@example.com"] passes the server schema and sends two identical attendee records to createMany, despite the dialog explicitly requiring unique emails. Deduplicate or reject repeated addresses on the server before constructing attendee records; client validation cannot enforce this invariant.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The removal tooltip is hard-coded in English, so users of other locales see “Remove email” while the surrounding add action and dialog are translated. Route this tooltip through t() and provide a corresponding translation entry.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: uniqueGuests filters against the preexisting attendees but never deduplicates guests themselves. Unlike the dialog schema, the server schema accepts repeated addresses, so a direct mutation with ["guest@example.com", "guest@example.com"] passes both through to createMany and creates duplicate attendees (or fails if constrained). Deduplicate the incoming list server-side before creating attendees.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The blacklist entries are explicitly lowercased, but guest is compared without the same normalization. A valid mixed-case address such as Blocked@Example.com therefore passes a blacklist containing blocked@example.com. Compare guest.toLowerCase() against the normalized blacklist.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines the role checks with &&, so a team administrator who is not also its owner fails this gate and receives FORBIDDEN unless independently an organizer or attendee. The intended admin-or-owner predicate must allow either check to succeed.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The sync branch returns a native fetch Response instead of the response shape expected by SDK- and Axios-based callers. WHY: Google reads res.data.access_token, Zoho reads tokenInfo.data.error, and HubSpot reads accessToken directly, so enabling synchronization causes token refresh failures or undefined token values. HOW: Parse the sync response and normalize it at each adapter boundary to the same shape returned by its refresh delegate.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Computed keys made from Zod schema toString() values do not validate or preserve arbitrary token response fields. WHY: The object parser strips real expiry and metadata fields such as expires_in, expiry_date, scope, and token_type; Zoom subsequently computes NaN expiry and Office365 loses refreshed expiry information. HOW: Declare the supported expiry fields explicitly and use passthrough() to retain provider-specific fields.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The credential update now stores the safeParse result envelope rather than the parsed token data. WHY: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns { success, data }, so the next GoogleCalendarService construction fails googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) because access_token and other token fields are nested under data, including when synchronization is disabled. HOW: Store the successful result's data property.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Bigin passes the credential record ID as the synchronization helper's userId argument. WHY: The helper sends this value as calcomUserId, requesting another user's tokens when IDs differ and routing team credentials through user synchronization as well. HOW: Thread credential.userId from biginAuth into refreshAccessToken and pass that value to refreshOAuthTokens.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new credential update references prisma without importing or declaring it. WHY: Searching this Salesforce module found only this usage, so type checking fails and executing the update raises ReferenceError. HOW: Import the Prisma client from @calcom/prisma.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: getClient now unconditionally refreshes Salesforce tokens and writes credentials on every service construction. WHY: The constructor always calls getClient, even for valid access tokens, adding a token-endpoint round trip and database write to each instance; the resulting jsforce connection still receives credentialKey.access_token rather than the refreshed token. HOW: Retain the existing jsforce-managed refresh flow or refresh only when necessary and initialize the connection with the refreshed token.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The webhook authenticates requests using a direct string inequality comparison against CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. String equality is not guaranteed to execute in constant time, exposing a timing oracle for the shared authentication secret on an endpoint that can overwrite user integration credentials. Validate that the supplied header is a string and compare fixed-length digests of the supplied and configured secrets with crypto.timingSafeEqual (or use an equivalent constant-time secret verification helper).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: These comments promise that arbitrary numeric properties are recognized as expiry and that other response properties are allowed. In a z.object shape, however, z.string().toString() produces a literal property name; it does not match arbitrary keys. Zod objects also strip unrecognized properties by default. Consequently an integrator following this documented minimum-response contract can lose the expiry field instead of having it recognized. Align the schema and comments by specifying the supported expiry fields and explicitly preserving additional fields.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the entire safeParse result ({ success: true, data: ... }), not the credential object returned by the previous schema.parse call. Passing that result as key stores a wrapper without top-level access_token, refresh_token or expiry_date, breaking subsequent loads even when sharing is disabled. Persist the successful result's data instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The sync branch returns a raw Fetch Response, but changed Google code reads res.data.access_token and Hubspot treats the return value as a HubspotToken; Zoho consumers likewise read .data. Enabling synchronization therefore makes these refreshes fail or consume undefined token fields. Adapt the sync response to each caller's expected representation (or normalize both branches and update all callers); do not return the same raw Response to both fetch-style and SDK-style consumers.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens declares its third argument as userId and serializes it as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint, but this call passes credentialId. Credential IDs are not user IDs, so synchronized refresh targets the wrong user or fails to find one. Pass the owning user's ID, preserving null for team-owned credentials.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The previous googleCredentialSchema.parse call returned the credential object itself, but parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result ({ success: true, data: ... }). Passing that wrapper as key stores credentials without top-level access_token/refresh_token fields, breaking subsequent credential loading even when sharing is disabled. Persist the helper result's data instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The sync branch returns an unparsed fetch Response, whereas the fallback preserves each provider's existing return contract. Google reads res.data, HubSpot expects a HubspotToken object, and Zoho/Bigin read tokenInfo.data. With syncing enabled these consumers receive a Response instead, so their refresh paths fail or read invalid token fields. Adapt the sync response at those consumers (Google/Zoho need a data envelope and HubSpot needs the parsed body), while preserving Response returns for consumers that already parse fetch responses.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens defines its third argument as userId and serializes it as calcomUserId, but this caller supplies credentialId. These IDs identify different records, so enabling sync requests another user's tokens or fails to locate the intended user. Pass the owning credential's userId (and preserve null for team credentials), rather than the credential record ID.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result ({ success: true, data: ... }), not the parsed credential object. Passing that entire result as Prisma's key replaces the stored Google credentials with a wrapper, so subsequent readers no longer find access_token, expiry_date, or refresh_token at the top level. Persist its data property instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The enabled sync branch returns a native fetch Response without decoding it. Google immediately reads res.data.access_token, Zoho reads tokenInfo.data.error, and HubSpot expects token properties directly. Those contracts worked with their original SDK/Axios return values, but a fetch Response supplies neither shape: Google and Zoho throw on undefined data and HubSpot receives undefined token fields. Decode the endpoint response and adapt it to each caller's expected shape (or normalize both helper paths and all callers to one token-data contract).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Computed property names using Zod schemas' toString() produce literal property names, not wildcard field validators. Consequently a normal response such as { access_token, expires_in } does not preserve expires_in: z.object strips unrecognized fields. In sync mode this loses the expiry required by Office365 and Zoom (and Google's expiry_date), leaving refreshed credentials without a usable updated expiration. Explicitly model the supported expiry fields and preserve additional provider fields with passthrough instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result ({ success, data }), whereas the previous schema.parse returned the credential object itself. Writing that wrapper to key removes access_token and refresh_token from the top-level stored credential, breaking subsequent authentication even when credential sharing is disabled. Persist the parsed data instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The sync branch returns a native fetch Response, but Google reads res.data, HubSpot reads token fields directly, and the Zoho consumers read response.data. With sharing enabled these consumers receive neither shape and token refresh fails. Decode and adapt the sync payload per integration (while preserving Response for the fetch-based consumers), rather than substituting a raw Response for every provider's return value.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: z.string().toString() is a literal object property name, not a wildcard for arbitrary response fields. Both computed keys normally stringify to the same name, so the latter overwrites the numeric validator. Because z.object strips unknown fields, normal expires_in/expiry_date fields are discarded (as is refresh_token) in sharing mode. Define the supported expiry fields explicitly and retain the required token fields instead of using schema instances as property names.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens names its third parameter userId and sends it as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint. This call instead passes credentialId. These independent IDs need not match, causing refresh requests for the wrong user (or no user) when sync is enabled. Pass the owning credential's userId, including null for team credentials.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new retry-count update inside catch throws if the reminder was deleted while scheduling was in progress. Booking cancellation or rescheduling can delete that row via deleteScheduledSMSReminder, so Prisma's missing-record error now escapes the per-reminder catch, aborts the cron request, and skips all remaining reminders. Use updateMany with the reminder ID so an already-deleted row is a no-op, and isolate persistence failures so they cannot escape the per-reminder error boundary.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The retry-count branch deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1, even if it has subsequently been scheduled successfully. A reminder that fails twice has count 2; if the next scheduling attempt succeeds (the cleanup and scheduling queries are separate, so concurrent invocations can reach this state), success sets referenceId but does not clear retryCount. The next cleanup deletes that future scheduled reminder, losing its tracking record. Restrict retry exhaustion cleanup to unscheduled SMS reminders rather than treating the count alone as sufficient for deletion.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The retry branch deletes rows regardless of whether they are now successfully scheduled. For example, after failures raise retryCount to 2, an already-running invocation can successfully schedule the SMS and save its referenceId; the next invocation still deletes that future reminder because success does not clear retryCount. This loses the record needed to track or cancel the scheduled SMS. Restrict retry exhaustion cleanup to unscheduled reminders (and clear the counter on success).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Both failure paths compute the next count from the earlier findMany snapshot. Two overlapping invocations reading retryCount 0 can both fail and write 1, so two failed attempts are recorded as only one and the exhaustion threshold is bypassed. Use Prisma's atomic increment in both failure updates rather than assigning a snapshot-derived count.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new backup-code branch accepts a valid backupCode even when an arbitrary nonempty totpCode has skipped password verification at lines 121–129. An attacker with a backup code can submit both fields and authenticate without knowing the account password, because this branch never validates the supplied TOTP. Ensure backup-code authentication verifies the password regardless of whether totpCode was also supplied.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Backup-code consumption overwrites the encrypted array using only the user id after validating a previously read snapshot. Concurrent requests can redeem the same code twice, and requests redeeming different codes can overwrite each other's removals and restore a consumed code. Use an atomic conditional update matching the original backupCodes value and reject or retry when no row is updated, or serialize redemption in a transaction with a row lock.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Successful enablement now changes only the modal step instead of notifying the parent that 2FA is enabled. Dismissing the backup-code screen through the dialog's onOpenChange path leaves viewer.me uninvalidated, so the settings switch still shows disabled and opens the enable flow rather than allowing disablement until a refresh. Invalidate the user's 2FA state when the enable request succeeds, independently of closing the backup-code display.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new authentication path checks a secret backup code with Array.indexOf. This performs ordinary string equality and stops at the first match, rather than providing constant-time secret comparison. Use fixed-length buffers with timingSafeEqual (reject invalid input lengths first), compare against every valid code without early exit, and retain the matching index for consumption. Apply the same correction to the backup-code check in the disable endpoint.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Backup-code verification and consumption are not atomic. Two requests can read the same stored list, both find the same code, and both successfully authenticate after writing the same updated list. Requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's removals, restoring one consumed code. This violates the stated guarantee that each backup code can be used exactly once. Consume with an atomic compare-and-swap against the original encrypted backupCodes value (and reject or retry if no row was updated), or use a transaction with appropriate locking.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The success toast is emitted independently of the clipboard write in EnableTwoFactorModal. Removing the write entirely, or copying incorrect codes, would leave this test passing. Read the clipboard after clicking and compare its contents with the displayed backup codes so the test verifies the copy operation rather than just its notification.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The download assertion verifies only the filename, which is fixed by the anchor's download attribute regardless of the blob contents. Generating an empty file or exporting incorrect backup codes would still pass. Inspect the downloaded file and compare its contents with the displayed codes to verify that the recovery material is actually exported.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The handler displays “Backup codes copied!” immediately, even if clipboard access is denied or writeText rejects. This can tell a user that their recovery codes are saved when nothing was copied. Await the clipboard write and show the success toast only after it resolves; handle failure without claiming success.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Two simultaneous requests can read the same backupCodes snapshot, both find the submitted code, and both successfully perform this unconditional update and authenticate. Requests consuming different codes can also overwrite each other's changes and restore a consumed code. Consume the code atomically, for example by conditionally updating against the original encrypted backupCodes value and rejecting or retrying when no row matches.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The successful enable response now only changes the step; onEnable is called exclusively by the backup-code Close button. The Dialog still passes dismissals directly to onOpenChange, so Escape or an outside dismissal after enabling bypasses onEnable even though server-side 2FA is already enabled. Ensure every exit from the post-success backup-code screen notifies the parent (or prevent dismissal until that explicit completion path).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The header conditional ends with `end if`, leaving an incomplete Ruby conditional modifier. WHY: Rendering the successful embed response fails with a template syntax error instead of displaying comments. HOW: Close the block with `end` alone.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Body extraction assumes every feed item has an Atom `content` field. WHY: SimpleRSS exposes ordinary RSS bodies as `description` or `content_encoded`, so valid RSS items without `content` fail at this line and abort the entire poll, including on-demand retrieval that invokes it. HOW: Select the available body using explicit hash keys, preferring full content, and handle items without any body before calling scrub.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Feed-supplied HTML is imported with raw_html cooking after only URL rewriting, without HTML sanitization. WHY: A script element or an image event handler in a feed body survives Nokogiri serialization, is stored verbatim by Post.cook, and executes in the forum origin when post.cooked is rendered as raw HTML. HOW: Sanitize imported HTML with the forum's safe HTML policy before storing it; URL absolutization is not a sanitizer.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: URL absolutization handles only leading-slash paths and treats protocol-relative URLs as local paths. WHY: An article containing `images/photo.jpg` loads the image relative to the forum embed route, while `//cdn.example/photo.jpg` is rewritten onto the article host, producing broken images and links. HOW: Resolve each nonblank href and src against the article URI with URI.join rather than manually concatenating the host.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Every missing article retrieval executes a complete feed poll inline before fetching the article. WHY: The retrieval throttle is keyed by article URL, so simultaneous loads of distinct articles each download and parse the same feed and run per-item database imports, multiplying feed-sized work across background workers instead of respecting the hourly polling schedule. HOW: Coordinate feed polling with a feed-scoped lock and freshness cache so article retrievals share one recent poll.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Retrieval is now asynchronous, but spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40-45 still expects TopicRetriever.new and retriever.retrieve during the controller request. Those expectations are no longer satisfied when jobs are queued, so the existing success test fails rather than testing the new contract. Update that spec to expect Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: nil, embed_url: embed_url), and test execution of the retriever separately in the job spec.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Unlike the surrounding translated labels, the visible post date uses strftime with a fixed day/month/year order and English abbreviated month names. Non-English forums therefore show untranslated dates. Use Rails' localisation helper with a locale-defined date format.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The URL is interpolated directly into both a single-quoted href and visible HTML. The prefix check only requires http(s), so a feed link containing a quote or markup can alter the attribution HTML. This becomes rendered content because import selects raw_html and Post#cook returns it without the rendering pipeline; parsing with Nokogiri does not escape injected elements or remove event attributes. Escape the URL for both contexts before building the link.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The conditional opened with `if` must close with `end`, not `end if`. ERB compiles this to an incomplete Ruby modifier-if expression, so rendering the successful embed view raises a template syntax error.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: RSS items commonly provide a description without a content element. For those items `i.content` is nil and calling `scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire polling run before this and subsequent items can be imported. Fall back to the description and handle items with neither field.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Two imports can both read no embed at line 15 before either commits. Each then creates a topic and attempts TopicEmbed.create! for the same URL; the unique index rejects the second insert with an unhandled uniqueness exception. The transaction rolls back its topic, but the import/job still fails. Serialize imports for a URL or rescue the uniqueness conflict outside the transaction and reload the winning embed.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This test expects TopicRetriever.new and retrieve during get :best, but the controller now only calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...). Those expectations remain unsatisfied, making the new controller test fail. Assert the enqueue and its arguments instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: absolutize_urls only rewrites values beginning with '/'. A source article at https://example.com/blog/article containing href='next.html' or src='images/photo.jpg' retains those values in the imported post, where they resolve against the Discourse origin instead of the source article. Resolve relative references against the complete source URL with URI.join; this also preserves the intended host of protocol-relative references.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: PollFeed passes decoded feed content directly to TopicEmbed.import, but the new import implementation explicitly sets cook_method to raw_html, and Post.cook returns raw unchanged for that method. Unlike import_remote's restricted Readability extraction, this path never filters script elements, event-handler attributes, or dangerous links. A malicious or compromised feed can therefore persist executable HTML into forum posts (and embed/best renders post.cooked with raw). Sanitize feed HTML with the application's HTML allowlist before passing it into this raw HTML import path, including on updates.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This request supplies neither an enabled embeddable_host nor an allowed referer. ensure_embeddable therefore rejects it before best reaches params.require(:embed_url). Removing the embed_url requirement would still leave this test green. Configure a valid host and matching referer first, then assert the missing-parameter response (including its expected status) so this case actually reaches the parameter validation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: feed_polling_enabled defaults to false, and this case only stubs the URL. execute therefore skips poll_feed regardless of whether it checks feed_polling_url at all. Enable polling and supply a valid embed_by_username in this case; otherwise deleting the URL guard would still pass this regression test.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This case leaves polling disabled and the feed URL blank, both of which independently prevent poll_feed. It consequently remains green if the embed_by_username guard is removed. Set polling enabled and a valid feed URL before stubbing the username to nil to isolate the behavior named by this test.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The category query indexes the first row without checking whether any row was returned. On installations without a stored embed_category setting, or whose configured category no longer exists, [0] is nil and ['id'] raises before the fallback can run, aborting the upgrade even when embedding is unused. Check for an empty result before reading the ID, and apply the same protection to the fallback query.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration inserts legacy host values verbatim instead of applying the normalization required by the new lookup. Existing URL-form entries such as https://example.com/1234 become database values that can never equal URI.host (example.com), disabling embedding for those hosts after upgrade. Normalize each migrated host by removing its scheme and path before insertion, consistently with EmbeddableHost's normalization.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: record_for_host compares URI.host against the saved host string even though the validator explicitly accepts a :port suffix. Saving example.com:8080 therefore succeeds, but a request from http://example.com:8080 resolves to example.com and is rejected, preventing embedding and category lookup for that configured host. Use a consistent port-aware representation for both stored entries and incoming URLs.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The domain comparison normalizes only the stored host. URI parsing preserves hostname case, so an allowed `example.com` does not match `https://EXAMPLE.com/article`, even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. This rejects legitimate embedding requests and makes category derivation fail for equivalent mixed-case URLs. Normalize the parsed hostname as well before comparing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This case claims to verify that a missing embeddable host prevents expansion, but the built topic has no TopicEmbed and the previous stub making has_topic_embed? true has been removed. Consequently the current implementation, which no longer checks for any allowed hosts, still passes this test because has_topic_embed? is false. Set embed_truncate to true and stub has_topic_embed? to true in this case so that absence of a host is the only false prerequisite; if absence of hosts is intentionally no longer a prerequisite, rename this case to describe the missing topic embed instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The join can return no rows (for example, when embed_category has no persisted setting or its stored name no longer matches a category). In that case execute(...)[0] is nil and indexing ['id'] aborts the migration, before the category_id == 0 fallback can run. Check whether the result has a first row before accessing its id; the fallback query below likewise needs to handle an empty result.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration inserts legacy host values verbatim, bypassing the normalization introduced in EmbeddableHost's before_validation callback. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host now compares URI.host (a bare hostname) against this stored value, so an existing entry such as `https://example.com/1234` will never match after upgrading. The changed embed controller tests explicitly exercise scheme/path-bearing configurations, but only through model creation, which runs the callback. Normalize migrated values to the same bare-host representation before inserting so existing embeds continue to work.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The old allowlist accepted URL-form entries (the existing embed controller tests used `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234`), but this INSERT preserves those strings verbatim and bypasses the new model's normalization callback. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` now compares only `URI(url).host` against the stored value, so those migrated hosts stop being allowed: existing embeds are denied and TopicRetriever rejects their URLs after upgrade. Normalize each legacy entry by stripping its scheme and path, consistently with the new model, before inserting it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The SELECT can return no rows when embed_category was never explicitly configured (or its category no longer exists). Accessing [0]['id'] then raises on nil, so the category_id == 0 fallback is never reached and upgrading fails even on installations not using embedding. Handle an empty result before dereferencing it, and likewise handle an absent uncategorized setting.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Legacy entries can include schemes and paths, as the changed embed controller tests demonstrate with http://discourse.org and https://example.com/1234. This raw SQL copy preserves those strings and bypasses the new model's normalization callback, but record_for_host compares the stored value to URI.host alone. Such previously working hosts stop allowing embeds after upgrade. Normalize each legacy entry to the same representation used by the reader before inserting it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The validator explicitly accepts example.com:8080 and the normalization callback preserves that port. URI.host for http://example.com:8080, however, is only example.com, so this query never finds the configured entry. Use a consistent authority representation at both the write and lookup sites so port-bearing allowed hosts actually work.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When embed_category has never been configured, or its saved name no longer matches a category, this SELECT returns no rows. Indexing [0] then ['id'] raises NoMethodError on nil before the intended category_id == 0 fallback can run. This blocks upgrades even on sites that never enabled embedding. Handle an absent row explicitly, and likewise handle an absent uncategorized setting row in the fallback.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The create endpoint assigns the supplied host directly, so a request with host: null reaches this callback with nil. Calling sub! raises NoMethodError before validates_format_of runs, producing a server error rather than the controller's render_json_error response. Guard the normalization so invalid absent hosts can be rejected by validation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new flex row makes the implicit Ember wrapper around header-extra-info a flex item, rather than .extra-info-wrapper inside it. For long topic titles, that outer div retains its automatic minimum width, so the overflow:hidden and ellipsis rules in desktop/topic-post.scss cannot shrink the flex item and the title pushes the navigation panel outside the header; the order applied to the nested .extra-info-wrapper also has no effect on the row. Apply the sizing/ordering constraints to the actual component root (including min-width: 0), or remove the implicit wrapper so .extra-info-wrapper itself becomes the flex item.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The second definition of downsize replaces the width/height definition rather than overloading it. Jobs::ResizeEmoji.execute still calls OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts), which now raises ArgumentError because the surviving method accepts at most four arguments, preventing emoji resizing. Use one method that supports both argument forms or give the geometry-based helper a distinct name.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new downsizing call passes only tempfile.path to animation detection, which checks whether that path ends in .GIF rather than checking filename. An oversized multipart GIF whose temporary path lacks that suffix takes downsize_instructions, whose input is explicitly restricted to frame zero, permanently discarding animation even when animated thumbnails are enabled. Preserve the image extension on the conversion input or pass explicit format information to animation selection.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The initial downsizing uses allow_animated_thumbnails even for avatar uploads. When allow_animated_avatars is enabled but allow_animated_thumbnails is disabled, an oversized GIF avatar is flattened before Upload.create_for reaches its avatar-specific conversion, so that later step cannot preserve its animation. Select allow_animated_avatars when type is avatar, matching Upload.create_for.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The fixed 10 MB limit replaces the configured attachment limit as well as the image limit in validateUploadedFile. Sites allowing attachments larger than 10 MB now have those otherwise permitted uploads rejected in the browser, although attachments cannot benefit from image downsizing. Apply the fixed input cap only to images and retain max_attachment_size_kb for attachments.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Ruby does not overload methods by argument count: this definition replaces the downsize method immediately above it. The existing ResizeEmoji caller in app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 still invokes OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts), which now raises ArgumentError (five arguments supplied to a method accepting three to four), preventing emoji resizing. Preserve the width/height API and give the geometry variant a distinct name, updating the new controller call accordingly.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Ruby does not overload methods by argument count: this second definition replaces the preceding downsize method. The existing ResizeEmoji caller at app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 invokes OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts), which now raises ArgumentError because the surviving method accepts only three or four arguments. Preserve the existing width/height API and give the geometry-string variant a separate name (updating the new controller caller accordingly), or implement explicit argument dispatch in a single method.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Ruby does not overload methods by arity: this definition replaces the width/height definition immediately above it. app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, so emoji resizing now raises ArgumentError instead of resizing the file. Preserve the old width/height entry point and give the geometry-string variant a distinct name (updating the upload controller accordingly), or explicitly dispatch both calling conventions in one method.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: totalPages adds an extra page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit. WHY: with 50 members and a limit of 50, Next remains enabled and requests offset 50, displaying an empty second page. HOW: use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), retaining the zero-member guard.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the public member endpoint now defaults all groups to 50 members, but the public group-members route and template have no pagination controls or subsequent fetch. WHY: ordinary groups with more than 50 members previously displayed their complete membership; now all members after the first 50 are inaccessible on the public membership page. HOW: add pagination to the public group-members route and template alongside this server-side limit.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: remove_member deletes the membership without clearing the removed user's primary_group_id. WHY: the previous usernames-based deletion path explicitly cleared this reference in Group#destroy_deletions; the new path leaves removed users displaying the former primary group's identity through post serializers. HOW: clear primary_group_id for this user when it equals the removed group ID, together with the membership deletion.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Applying a default limit of 50 to every group changes the public members-page contract: custom groups previously returned all members. The updated public group-members route calls findMembers() once with the model's default limit of 50, and its template only iterates members; unlike the admin page, it provides no next/previous actions or further fetching. Consequently members after the first 50 are inaccessible on the public page (and automatic groups previously showed up to 200). Update the public consumer to support pagination alongside this server change.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: For a nonzero member count exactly divisible by the limit, floor(count / limit) + 1 overcounts by one. For example, 50 members with limit 50 displays 1/2 and enables Next; clicking it requests offset 50 and shows an empty member list. Use ceiling division so the last populated page disables Next.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When user_count is exactly divisible by limit (for example, 50 members with limit 50), this computes two pages instead of one. showingLast remains false on the actual last page, so next sets offset to 50 and loads an empty member list, displaying page 2/2 despite the group having only one page. Use ceiling division so that every advertised page contains members for a positive count.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The changed members endpoint now limits every group to 50 users, including custom groups that previously returned all members. This public route calls findMembers only once, and the corresponding public template only iterates members; the next/previous actions added in this PR belong to the admin controller. Consequently, users visiting a custom group with more than 50 members cannot view the remaining members. Add public pagination (or fetch subsequent pages) to match the new endpoint contract.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When user_count is a positive multiple of limit (for example 50 members with limit 50), floor(count / limit) + 1 overstates the page count. showingLast remains false on the actual final page, allowing Next to load an empty page. Use ceiling division instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new-group form exposes alias_level and Group.asJSON sends it in the create request, but this action assigns only name and visible before saving. A group created with a nondefault alias level silently retains the default despite the successful save. Assign alias_level here as in update.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Fallback locales are explicitly loaded only in the controller callback, leaving background translations without their fallback files. WHY: Jobs::Base sets I18n.locale and executes jobs without this callback, and translate_accelerator loads only config.locale; on a fresh worker using a non-English site locale, missing keys cannot fall back to English because backend fallback calls bypass the accelerator. HOW: Ensure the full fallback list is loaded at the shared translation entry point rather than relying exclusively on the HTTP controller callback.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The fallback result now depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the shared accelerator cache does not include that setting or the current site in its key. WHY: translate_accelerator caches no-argument translations by key, current locale and backend identity only, so multisite requests using the same user locale but different site defaults reuse the first site's fallback text; changing the default locale also leaves cached fallback text stale. HOW: Include the effective fallback chain in the translation cache key so cached results are isolated by fallback configuration.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: TagDevice caches a device ID before CreateOrUpdateDevice checks the limit, so the new authentication check rejects only the first request for an over-limit device. Repeating the request with the same X-Grafana-Device-Id hits tagDeviceUI's cache and returns nil, allowing Authenticate to issue an anonymous identity despite the full device limit. Cache the device only after successful persistence, and ensure concurrent requests cannot interpret an in-progress admission as a successful one.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new limit enforcement treats TagDevice returning nil as successful admission even when the request has no device header. TagDevice immediately returns nil for an empty X-Grafana-Device-Id, so a client can omit that header and continue authenticating and accessing anonymous APIs after the configured limit is reached. Establish an enforceable device identity for requests subject to the limit instead of treating missing identification as admission.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The active-device count is checked separately from the subsequent insert without a transaction or shared admission lock. Two requests for different device IDs can both observe one remaining slot and both insert successfully, exceeding the configured limit; the unique device_id constraint does not prevent this. Serialize the count-and-admit operation across Grafana instances using database-level admission locking or equivalent atomic enforcement.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The count check is not atomic with the insertion that follows it. For example, with deviceLimit=1 and no devices, two concurrent requests for different device IDs can both read count=0, both pass this branch, and both insert successfully. This violates the configured anonymous-device limit (and can occur across server instances). Serialize admission with a database-backed lock or an appropriately isolated transaction covering both the count and insertion; a process-local mutex alone would not protect multi-instance deployments. Add a concurrent-registration test asserting that only the available number of slots can be admitted.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: tagDeviceUI populates localCache before attempting persistence (line 87), while cache hits return without retrying persistence. When the new limit check rejects a device, this return propagates the error for only its first request: subsequent requests with the same device key hit the cache and authenticate successfully for the cache lifetime. Cache only successfully persisted devices, or remove the cache entry when tagging fails, so a rejected device cannot bypass the configured limit by retrying.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The count and subsequent upsert are separate database operations with no serialization. When one slot remains, two requests for different new devices can both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert successfully. The configured admission limit therefore does not hold under concurrent requests (including across server instances). Make the capacity check and insertion atomic with database-level serialization appropriate to the supported databases.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Both observation paths convert to float64 only after integer division by time.Millisecond (here and at line 136). Requests shorter than 1 ms are therefore recorded as zero, and all other durations are truncated to whole milliseconds. This makes the fractional millisecond buckets declared above misleading and systematically understates latency. Divide floating-point durations instead in both paths.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The returned middleware factory shares a single MetricsMiddleware, including its mutable next pointer. If it is applied to client A and then client B, both decorated clients now forward requests to B. If another chain wraps the first decorated client, this can even create a forwarding cycle. Concurrent construction and requests additionally race on next. Share the registered metrics, but allocate a separate middleware wrapper for each application of the factory.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The Prometheus HELP text says this histogram measures sizes returned, but QueryData observes len(v.JSON) from incoming queries and CallResource observes len(req.Body), both before calling the plugin. Operators reading the exported metric documentation can therefore mistake request payload sizes for response sizes. Describe incoming request payload sizes instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Both QueryData and CallResource cases send empty payloads, and this assertion only checks that the histogram has at least one sample. Replacing either size calculation with constant zero would therefore leave the test green. Supply nonempty query JSON and resource bodies and assert the size histogram's SampleSum against their expected byte lengths, so incorrect size instrumentation fails the test.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The asynchronous legacy write derives its timeout from the original request context, as do the other three write goroutines. WHY: Once the handler returns, request cancellation cancels this child context too, so successful unified writes can consistently fail to reach legacy storage despite the nominal ten-second timeout. HOW: Detach cancellation with context.WithoutCancel(ctx) before applying the bounded timeout, preserving request values needed for tenant identity.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Legacy Update receives the original UpdatedObjectInfo rather than the object successfully committed to unified storage. WHY: Playlist legacy Update invokes UpdatedObject(ctx, old) against its own stored object, so a patch applied to stale legacy data can persist a different result or fail its preconditions instead of mirroring the successful unified update. HOW: Restore the updateWrapper around res so the legacy layer receives the committed unified object rather than recomputing the transformation.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Successful Delete records the resource name in the histogram's kind label. WHY: recordStorageDuration passes that argument directly to WithLabelValues, creating a retained histogram per distinct deleted object and unbounded metric cardinality over the server lifetime. HOW: Pass options.Kind, consistent with the error branch and other operations.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The legacy DeleteCollection duration and error are recorded in the unified-storage histogram. WHY: Each successful unified deletion contributes a second storage observation for a different backend, while legacy failures appear as unified failures and the legacy histogram receives no observation. HOW: Record this result with recordLegacyDuration.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: A unified Create failure is recorded with recordLegacyDuration; Update repeats the same collector error at line 129. WHY: Unified write failures disappear from the storage failure histogram and are attributed to legacy even though the legacy operation is never attempted. HOW: Use recordStorageDuration in both unified error branches.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This test name says creation occurs only in the unified store, but the case configures Legacy.Create and mode 3 invokes both Storage.Create and Legacy.Create. The resulting test output describes the opposite storage contract and can mislead maintainers about expected dual-write behaviour. Rename it to describe creation in both stores.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Create now returns before Legacy.Create finishes, but the background operation still inherits the request context. When the API handler returns, that context is canceled, canceling the legacy write even though its ten-second timeout has not elapsed. Previously the synchronous call completed before the request ended. The same lifecycle mismatch affects Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection. Detach request cancellation while retaining context values before starting these background writes, then apply the bounded timeout, so successful requests do not routinely leave legacy storage unchanged.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The successful Create and Update cases configure legacy mock responses but never assert that those calls occur, and all four write tests return after checking only the unified-store result. Since the implementation performs legacy writes in goroutines, the assertions can finish before those calls even start. Removing the legacy goroutines from Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection would still pass these tests, leaving the defining dual-write behavior untested. Add separate legacy-call signals, wait for their completion with a bounded condition-based wait, and assert the legacy calls and arguments (using distinct legacy and storage mocks). Mock response setup alone does not verify execution.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Create records a failed Storage.Create using recordLegacyDuration, even though Legacy.Create is never attempted on this path. Update repeats this at line 129. This hides unified-storage failures from its duration/error series and adds fictitious failures to the legacy series. Use recordStorageDuration in both error paths.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This observation times Legacy.DeleteCollection but calls recordStorageDuration. Each successful collection deletion therefore contributes two observations to unified-storage timing and none to legacy timing, and legacy errors are attributed to the wrong backend. Record this with recordLegacyDuration.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The successful Storage.Delete observation passes name, whereas its failure path and the legacy observation pass options.Kind in the same argument position. Successes and failures for the same operation consequently land in different label series, and individual resource names introduce potentially unbounded cardinality. Use options.Kind consistently.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Delete builds log with name, kind and method but puts d.Log into the context instead. Logs emitted by either storage implementation through the context lose those correlation fields, unlike the other methods. Pass the enriched log to NewContext.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The independently launched legacy writes do not preserve the order of primary mutations, even when the client issues requests sequentially. For example, after Create returns successfully, a client can Delete the same object; the delete goroutine can reach Legacy.Delete before this goroutine reaches Legacy.Create. The delete then finds nothing, and the delayed create leaves an object in legacy storage that no longer exists in primary storage. Two updates can similarly overwrite a newer legacy value with an older one. Preserve per-object mutation order (including across create/update/delete), or keep the legacy calls synchronous rather than launching independent goroutines.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The background write still derives its context from the HTTP request. Once Create returns and the response completes, that context is canceled; WithTimeoutCause does not detach cancellation, so the legacy write can fail immediately or be canceled in flight despite the successful unified write. The same issue affects the other new background mutations. Detach cancellation while preserving context values before applying the bounded timeout, or await replication before returning.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Independent goroutines do not preserve mutation order across requests. For example, unified Create succeeds and returns while its legacy Create is delayed; a subsequent Delete succeeds in unified storage and its legacy Delete runs first, finding nothing; the delayed legacy Create then inserts the object. Unified storage now has no object while legacy storage retains it. Updates can similarly arrive in reverse order. Preserve per-resource mutation ordering (including create/delete), or keep replication synchronous rather than launching independent goroutines.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: BuildIndex now leaves the cache unlocked throughout construction, so GetIndex can return nil for a key whose index is already being built. Concurrent Search calls or Search racing with handleEvent can therefore build separate indexes for the same key; the last cache assignment replaces the other index, potentially discarding updates written by the event handler, and repeats the full resource scan. Serialize builds per NamespacedResource and recheck the cache after acquiring that key's lock, while allowing different keys to build concurrently.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new TotalDocs call iterates Bleve's cache without a read lock after the write-event consumer has already started. A write event for an uncached namespace can call getOrCreateIndex and publish an index while TotalDocs ranges over the map, causing a data race and potentially a fatal concurrent map iteration/write error during startup. Protect the cache iteration in bleveBackend.TotalDocs with cacheMu.RLock/RUnlock.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new list item passes only promRule, but RuleActionsButtons.V2 still renders SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. Clicking the newly enabled Silence notifications menu item sets showSilenceDrawer without rendering any drawer, so silencing from either list view no longer works. Adapt the drawer path to accept the Prometheus rule UID or load the ruler rule on demand.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: canDelete now accepts Prometheus-rule permissions, but the delete menu item still requires rulerRule at line 165. Both new Grafana list paths omit rulerRule, so authorized users lose the Delete action despite canDelete being true. Render deletion using the identifier-based handler for Prometheus-only rules instead of requiring a ruler DTO.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: canPause now accepts Prometheus-rule permissions, but rendering MenuItemPauseRule still requires a Grafana rulerRule at line 123. The new Grafana list items never supply that prop, so pause and resume disappear from the list even for editable alert rules. Provide a Prometheus-compatible pause action or fetch the required ruler DTO on demand.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to a hook that hardcodes isFederated to false, discarding the previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check. Legacy RuleActionsButtons uses this wrapper for Update, so federated Mimir rules with source_tenants now receive an Edit action even though they were explicitly immutable before this change. Preserve the combined rule's federation status when computing its abilities.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously checked isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group), so callers could rely on Update and Delete being unsupported for federated Mimir groups. This delegation passes only the ruler rule and identifier to an implementation that hardcodes isFederated = false. Consequently existing combined-rule consumers now advertise editing and deleting federated rules whenever datasource permissions allow it. Preserve the federation check in this wrapper or pass the group federation state into the delegated ability calculation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Finding the rule row waits for the Prometheus response, not the folder-permission response. GrafanaRuleListItem renders its row immediately, whereas useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable initially has no folder and returns isEditable=false. Thus this negative assertion can pass during loading even if the resolved folder permissions are ignored and editing is subsequently allowed. Wait for the folder permission lookup to complete (for example using an observable request-completion signal and flushing its React update) before asserting that Edit is absent, so a regression that grants editing after loading fails this test.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: skipToken is converted to undefined, but the underlying hook treats an absent rule as supported once loading is false and grants Duplicate from Grafana create permission. AlertRuleMenu ORs this result with the ruler result, so a datasource rule with duplication unsupported or denied can acquire a Duplicate action simply because the user can create Grafana rules. Return neutral abilities for skipToken after calling the hook.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The previous implementation checked isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) before allowing Update and Delete. Delegating directly to useAllRulerRuleAbilities now loses that group information; the delegated hook explicitly sets isFederated=false. Existing CombinedRule consumers therefore receive editable/removable abilities for federated groups when ordinary datasource permissions allow them. Preserve the group-level immutability check in this wrapper or pass it to the delegated hook.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: AlertRuleMenu passes skipToken for datasource rules and ORs these results with the ruler permissions. However, converting skipToken to undefined does not disable abilities: the new calculator treats an absent rule as non-loading and non-plugin-provided, so Duplicate is supported and allowed whenever the user has Grafana rule-create permission. A datasource rule whose own Duplicate permission is denied can therefore still show that action. Return neutral [false, false] abilities for skipped inputs (in both singular and plural wrappers), while still calling hooks unconditionally.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new encoder records client-credentials access tokens with the unknown grant shortcut `na` instead of `cc`. ClientCredentialsGrantType.process creates its ClientSessionContext and directly invokes responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken() without passing through OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse or setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE, so every client-credentials token loses the grant information this change promises. Set Constants.GRANT_TYPE to context.getGrantType() on that client-session context before generating the access token.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The matcher reads the wrong character range and rejects equality rather than inequality when checking the grant shortcut. The encoder places the grant at indices 4–5, so a token with an incorrect grant (including `na`) still passes the authorization-code, refresh, device and CIBA event assertions whenever its suffix resembles a UUID. Validate the six-character context length and require substring(4, 6) to equal the expected shortcut.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The encoder in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider produces two session characters, two token-type characters, and then two grant characters. This matcher instead reads substring(3, 5), and returns false on equality rather than on a mismatch. Consequently, the updated code-to-token, refresh, device and CIBA assertions can all pass with an incorrect grant encoded in the token ID, hiding regressions in grant propagation. Check the six-character prefix length and compare substring(4, 6) against the expected grant, rejecting mismatches.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The encoder places the two-character grant shortcut at offsets 4–6, but this matcher extracts offsets 3–5 and rejects matching values rather than mismatches. Consequently an ID with the wrong grant (or any other prefix with a UUID suffix) can pass these event assertions. Check the prefix length and reject when substring(4, 6) does not equal the expected shortcut.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The check labeled 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' actually checks grantType again. A null rawTokenId therefore passes construction and encodeTokenId turns it into the literal suffix ':null', rather than rejecting the invalid token ID.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The decoder requires a six-character prefix (two characters per field), but getShortcut() is accepted without length validation; the new interface even documents three-letter shortcuts as normal. A custom grant returning three characters successfully issues tokens whose IDs subsequently throw IllegalArgumentException when decoded. Validate exactly two characters when registering shortcuts, including lazy registration, and align the interface contract.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The lazy registration path bypasses the uniqueness constraint enforced at startup. If a newly deployed grant uses an existing shortcut, this put replaces the old grant's reverse mapping while its forward mapping remains cached. Previously issued tokens then decode as the new grant, and both grants issue indistinguishable context prefixes. Reserve shortcuts with putIfAbsent and reject conflicting owners before adding the forward entry; apply the same rule to the decoder's lazy refresh path.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new API documentation recommends a three-letter shortcut, whereas getTokenContextFromTokenId requires a six-character context and reserves exactly two characters for the grant shortcut. An extension author following this contract will issue IDs that this decoder rejects. Document the two-character requirement explicitly.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: isAccessTokenId(expectedGrantShortcut) claims to match the expected grant, but it compares characters 3–4 rather than 4–5 and returns false on equality. Consequently a valid UUID suffix can pass even with the wrong grant, undermining the newly updated event assertions. Extract positions 4–6 and reject inequality, with a prefix-length check.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The grant occupies indices 4–5 in the encoder's six-character prefix, but this condition examines indices 3–4 and rejects equality rather than inequality. Consequently IDs such as onrtna:<valid UUID> pass even when the event expects authorization_code, masking missing or incorrect grant propagation in all four changed event assertions. Compare substring(4, 6) to the expected shortcut and reject a mismatch (with a prefix-length guard).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Catching RuntimeException allows an unrelated failure to satisfy the invalid-grant test. In this fixture the factory never receives postInit, so its sessionFactory is null; looking up the absent ac shortcut enters getGrantTypeByShortcut's fallback and throws NullPointerException before the decoder can perform its intended IllegalArgumentException rejection. Initialize/mock the fallback factory and catch only IllegalArgumentException so removing the explicit unknown-grant validation cannot leave this test green through an unrelated exception.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The encoded prefix places the grant shortcut at indices 4 and 5, after two session and two token characters. substring(3, 5) instead reads the final token-type character and first grant character (for example 'ta' from 'onrtac'). Consequently these event assertions do not verify the grant encoded by the writer. Extract substring(4, 6), guarding the prefix length before slicing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The condition returns false when the extracted shortcut equals the expected shortcut. This inverts the assertion: even after correcting the extraction indices, valid tokens will fail and tokens carrying another grant will pass as long as their suffix is a UUID. Return false when the shortcut does not equal the expected value.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test asserts caughtExceptions without waiting for the reader thread to finish. A listing request already in flight when deletedAll is set can fail and append its exception after the assertion has passed, allowing the concurrency regression this test targets to go undetected. Keep a reference to the reader thread and join it before asserting the collected exceptions.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The reader's stop flag is set only after every group deletion succeeds. If remove() throws, the test exits while its non-daemon reader continues issuing requests indefinitely and accumulating exceptions, leaking a thread and load into subsequent tests. Set the stop flag in a finally block and wait for the reader to terminate on both success and failure.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The reader can still be inside groups() when deletedAll is set. The main thread immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty, so a failing in-flight request can add its exception after the assertion and the test incorrectly passes. Retain the reader thread and join it after signaling termination, before checking caughtExceptions, so the assertion includes every read performed by the test.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Setting deletedAll does not wait for a request already executing on the reader thread. That request can fail during deletion, while the main thread sets the flag and asserts an empty list before the catch block adds the exception. The regression test then passes despite the failure it is meant to detect. Retain the reader thread and join it before examining caughtExceptions.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: If any remove() throws, execution skips deletedAll.set(true). The reader continues issuing requests and catching exceptions indefinitely, including after realm/client teardown, and its non-daemon thread can prevent JVM shutdown. Put the deletion loop in try/finally so the stop flag is set and the reader is awaited even when deletion fails.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Setting deletedAll only requests that the reader stop; it does not wait for the current groups() request or its catch block. If that request fails due to the deleted-group regression, assertThat can observe an empty list and pass before the exception is appended.
