When a partition reassignment closes the old strategy and calls create_with_partitions again on the same factory, create_thread_queue_parallel_worker passes this same stopped pool to the new strategy. Its workers have exited and its queues are shut down, so processing cannot resume (and submit's exception handler can mark rejected messages complete). Previously factory-owned parallel resources survived individual strategy closure until factory.shutdown. Keep the pool alive across strategy replacement, or create a fresh pool for each strategy and isolate its offset tracker.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The factory creates its queue_pool only once in __init__ and supplies it to every strategy, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() and terminate() both call queue_pool.shutdown(). When a rebalance closes the old strategy and calls create_with_partitions again on this factory, the new strategy receives the already-shut-down queues and workers. Submissions then fail (and the submission exception handler marks those offsets complete), so the consumer can commit results it never processes. Give each replacement strategy a fresh pool, or align pool ownership so closing a strategy does not destroy a factory-owned reusable pool.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When result_processor raises, the exception is logged but the finally block still completes its offset. The commit thread can then commit past this failed message, permanently skipping it after restart. For example, offset 100 fails and 101 succeeds; both leave outstanding and 102 becomes the committed next offset. This violates the strategy's explicit guarantee that offsets are committed only after successful processing. Surface processing failure to the strategy and leave the failed offset outstanding until it is successfully retried or explicitly handled.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: close() shuts down the pool owned by ResultsStrategyFactory, but create_thread_queue_parallel_worker() reuses that same pool for the next strategy. On a partition reassignment, closing the old strategy stops its workers and shuts its queues; the replacement strategy then submits to those shut queues. put() raises, and submit's broad exception handler marks the message complete anyway, allowing unprocessed messages to be committed. Give each strategy a fresh pool and tracker, or implement a lifecycle that drains and resets the shared pool before reuse; do not reuse a shut-down pool.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Kafka offsets can legitimately contain gaps (for example after compaction or transactional records). Iterating every integer and breaking when it is absent treats an undelivered offset as unfinished work. For received and completed offsets 100, 102, 103, this scan initially commits only 100 rather than 103; progress then depends on another commit-loop iteration and cleanup changing min_offset. Track ordering over received offsets instead: stop at the first outstanding received offset, not at a missing integer. The new gap tests encode the same invalid assumption and should cover legitimate broker gaps instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: complete_offset runs in finally even when result_processor raises. Thus a transient processing failure becomes eligible for commit on the next commit-loop iteration, permanently skipping the failed result. This contradicts the successful-processing guarantee; the error-handling test only checks before the one-second commit timer typically fires. Mark completion only on success and propagate or otherwise retain failures for retry.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The pool is created once on ResultsStrategyFactory and passed to every new strategy, but strategy.close shuts that pool down. When a partition reassignment closes the old strategy and creates another from the same factory, the new strategy receives queues whose workers have exited (and whose queues are shut down). Results can no longer be processed. Give each strategy a fresh pool or preserve the factory-owned pool through strategy replacement with appropriate draining and offset-state isolation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The claim that offsets are committed only after successful processing is false: OrderedQueueWorker catches processor exceptions and calls complete_offset in finally, so the commit loop treats failed items as completed too. submit also marks offsets complete after exceptions. This contract can lead callers to rely on retries that do not occur. Document the actual log-and-skip behavior rather than promising successful-only commits.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The strategy promises natural backpressure when queues fill, but FixedQueuePool constructs queue.Queue() without a capacity and submit unconditionally puts items into it. These queues never become full and no MessageRejected or other producer throttling occurs. Remove this guarantee or explicitly describe the unbounded buffering so operators do not rely on nonexistent memory protection.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new ZADD writes sorted sets under the same keys that the previous implementation populated with Redis sets. Existing buffered traces therefore raise WRONGTYPE on insertion, and the new ZSCAN also fails when the flusher encounters an old queued segment, interrupting ingestion and flushing during deployment until those keys disappear. Version the buffer and associated queue namespace or provide an explicit migration/drain strategy before switching command types.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: ZUNIONSTORE uses the default SUM aggregation, so a payload present in both merge inputs receives the sum of its end timestamps rather than its actual end timestamp. Replaying a child already merged into the root can recreate it in its original parent buffer; merging that buffer into the root then gives the replayed span an inflated score, retaining older duplicates ahead of newer spans during eviction. Use AGGREGATE MAX on both union operations to preserve timestamp scores.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Removing the max_segment_spans check makes the constructor's configured span limit ineffective. The replacement Lua truncation always uses 1000, independently of self.max_segment_spans, so a buffer configured with a lower limit now emits segments exceeding that limit, while a higher limit still loses spans at 1000. Pass the configured limit into the script and use it for truncation, or retain explicit enforcement of the configured limit.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: buffer.py now writes end_timestamp_precise as each payload's score, and the new zpopmin eviction depends on those scores remaining timestamps. ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM: if the same payload is present in both sets (for example from replaying a span after its parent redirects to a different set), its timestamp is doubled. Such old duplicates then outrank genuinely newer spans and survive eviction incorrectly. Use AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) on both union calls so merging preserves the timestamp contract.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new ZADD uses the same `span-buf:s:` keys that the previous version populated with SADD. Any segment still buffered when this version deploys causes Redis WRONGTYPE errors on writes (and ZSCAN/ZCARD also fail on those keys). Rolling deployment also lets old workers create sets while new workers expect sorted sets. Use a versioned key namespace consistently across writers, Lua, queues and readers, or provide a coordinated migration/drain before switching types.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM. If a payload is present in both sets—for example a replay writes a child back into its original parent set after it was already merged into the resolved ancestor—its end-timestamp score is doubled during this merge. The resulting score is no longer an end timestamp, so ZPOPMIN retains replayed older spans ahead of newer spans when enforcing the 1,000-span cap. Specify AGGREGATE MAX (also on the second ZUNIONSTORE) to preserve timestamp scores for duplicate members.
